static_traits.name: Kristin Bowman
static_traits.family_status: Father has passed away; boyfriend serving in the military
static_traits.social_status: Supportive boyfriend and several close friends, but not yet opened up to them about Self-doubt and feelings of not being worthy
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past; no similar psychological issues have emerged before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, highly cooperative, capable of self-Reflection, calm tone

basic_info.main_problem: Because I made a mistake in a piano solo recital, I feel I do not deserve recognition or applause, which affects my self-esteem and confidence.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize I have a thinking pattern of negating the positive and focusing on mistakes, which hinders my musical growth and causes emotional distress, so I am seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: A piano solo recital several months ago: a mistake occurred in the final section of the performance. Since then the client has kept ruminating on this mistake, believing it ruined the entire recital, Feeling embarrassed and ashamed; although the audience applauded and gave positive comments afterward, the client still struggles to see the positive side of the performance, often feels Anxiety and pressure when playing, has Decreased drive, and tries to cope by doubling practice and seeking comfort from peers. This event became a turning point for their self-worth and Damaged confidence.
Death of father: Father has passed away (specific time and details Not mentioned).

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of recognition / do not deserve applause
Only with a perfect, flawless performance do I have worth and deserve recognition

special_situations.event: In the last piano solo concert, a mistake occurred in the final section, yet the audience still gave applause and positive comments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a single mistake occurs during the performance, I ruin the whole show and do not deserve any recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling practice, seeking comfort and recognition from peers, negating positive feedback to push myself toward greater perfection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: All this applause does not belong to me; I do not deserve recognition

special_situations.event: Every time I sit at the piano or go on stage, memories of that mistake flood back with intense Anxiety and pressure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make another mistake, everyone will think I am not good enough and I will ruin the entire performance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive Self-monitoring and tense preparation before performances, trying hard to control everything to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely make mistakes this time; everyone will be disappointed

special_situations.event: The audience's applause and positive feedback after the show; no one dwells on that mistake the way I do
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only a perfect, flawless performance counts as success and deserves recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessively replays mistake clips in mind, ignoring positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Even when they applaud, I have failed

special_situations.event: With a new solo recital approaching, Thinking about possibly making mistakes again causes Anxiety in advance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not completely perfect this time, I will ruin the whole recital again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Overtime-style practicing and constantly seeking reassurance from others for peace of mind
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: One mistake and the whole thing is ruined

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and seen and to gain affirmation through performance
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated and humiliated over mistakes, with self-worth destroyed
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of criticism through perfectionism and Self-monitoring
Maintains suspicion toward positive feedback to avoid disappointment and shame

object_relations.self_representation: Someone who does not deserve applause, a failure who easily 'messes up' the whole show
object_relations.object_representation: The audience/others are judges who will be disappointed and criticize me at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing mistakes in a performance or hearing positive feedback about her performance
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Projecting inner self-criticism outward, believing the audience and others are disappointed in and criticizing me
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain a gentle, Empathy tone; avoid directly refuting their feelings; use open-ended Questioning to invite distinguishing facts from speculation, encouraging connection with their own emotions and examination of evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about honestly expressing Self-doubt and feelings of not deserving to my boyfriend or friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing expression will burden others or be negated, thus choosing to suppress and not speak
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle tone, allowing pauses and Silence; invite the client to identify suppressed emotions and bodily sensations, exploring feasible boundaries for moderate expression and support resources.

manifestations: Tying self-worth to 'perfect and flawless', negating the entire performance and applause over a single mistake
Finds it hard to accept positive feedback, doubts the meaning of recognition
Despite having a supportive boyfriend and friends, not yet opened up to them about Self-doubt and feelings of not being worthy

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Insists on the inner rule 'only perfection deserves recognition'
Negating applause and positive feedback with strict self-demands

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy their original desire would send outward onto themselves, restraining expression toward others or seeking help, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not expressing genuine Self-doubt and feelings of not deserving to boyfriend and friends
Turning criticism and pressure against the self, with inner self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believes he has disappointed everyone and others will criticize him

positive_force: Having professional competence and stage experience, performing well in most parts of the show and receiving applause and positive feedback
Able to engage in self-Reflection and willing to try new cognitive restructuring approaches
Having a supportive boyfriend and several close friends
Has empathy for others (can view others' mistakes more tolerantly)
negative_force: Negating the positive and mental filtering, over-focusing on mistakes
Future-oriented worrying leads to Anxiety before and after performances
Over-relying on external comfort and recognition to ease unease
Not opening up to the support system, Relationship tension

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly replaying mistakes and negating positive feedback when playing piano or around performances
antecedent: Sitting at the piano to practice or perform on stage
Recalling that mistake during a performance months ago
target_behavior.core_reason: Binds self-worth to perfect performance, black-and-white thinking and mental filtering exist, leading to catastrophic focus on mistakes
target_behavior.function: Trying to avoid criticism, maintaining a sense of control over mistakes, short-term relief from uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Performance Anxiety and Increased stress, lowered self-esteem and Decreased drive, subjective experience dominated by negative information

target_behavior.behavior: Frequently seeks comfort and approval from peers (reassurance seeking)
antecedent: When feeling Anxiety and Self-doubt before or after performances
target_behavior.core_reason: Dependence on external validation, unstable inner self-worth
target_behavior.function: Gaining short-term reassurance and affirmation to ease Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Dependence on external comfort increases, confidence is hard to internalize, and the problem persists
